### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `15b55e02d1647cbb0fd1d8a0d13bfd4a3e6ba105` — the merge of head `a385bcf08b2b01af0e15a53af316269325c86532` into base `4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 15b55e02d1647cbb0fd1d8a0d13bfd4a3e6ba105 && git checkout 15b55e02d1647cbb0fd1d8a0d13bfd4a3e6ba105
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 a385bcf08b2b01af0e15a53af316269325c86532 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 && git merge --no-ff a385bcf08b2b01af0e15a53af316269325c86532

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `a385bcf08b2b01af0e15a53af316269325c86532` (Fixes #37954). Full read · 2026-11-27T16:43Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** 5 files, +715/-12, of which 388 lines are the new test file. Check-runs at a385bcf0: 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed. Mergeable state is clean. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. `l1-face` is CLEAN on 13 items. No contract review is owed: no published schema, no governed path, and no narrowing (see (2) below).

**What I read myself.**
- **One trigger per kernel.** `startRecordHooks` runs only in the `kernel:ready` branch where `realtime` is absent, after the existing `enableEventSync === false` return. So an opted-out kernel registers nothing, and a realtime kernel is unchanged. The objects come from `guardedObjectsFor`, which reads through `objectSourcesFor`, so a source with `refresh.onRecordChange: false` is left out, as the docs say. `onSourcesChanged` re-syncs on a no-op until the hooks have started.
- **No unit opened for the write.** The hooks are registered in code with no `meta`, so `opensAfterAbortUnit` (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:537`) opens no unit around an indexed object's writes. This follows the #22782 line, and the hooks add no transaction to a write that had none.
- **Ids.** A batch insert dispatches `afterInsert` once per row with `rowCtx.result` set to the row (`engine-insert.ts:1674-1678`), so `rowOf` never sees an array. A predicate update or delete arrives per row with `input.id` bound. The copy is taken before `stripSearchCompanion` runs on the result, and the service re-reads by id anyway.
- **`deferRecordSync`.** It goes through `runAfterOpenUnitsCommit` when the engine has it, and starts at once otherwise. A rejection is caught with a backstop warning, so the hook never throws and never awaits. `stop()` uses `unregisterHooksByPackage` with the package id. The seam is the single place #37735's queue will replace.
- **Tests.** The nine no-realtime cases cover each changeset bullet except the restore gap: boot line, create and update, delete, a slow embedder off the response, sync after commit, no sync on rollback, a predicate write per row, a late source, and teardown. The realtime describe pins "each write synced once". There are five ablations in the report.
- **Prose.** The changeset, the `knowledge.mdx` section and the plugin jsdoc are true sentence by sentence against the code above and the engine they cite.

**Points.**
- **(1) Route.** The predicate write is synced row by row, not through `requestReconcile`. I agree with the area's A: the engine already gives one after-hook per matched row, and the case "a predicate write is synced row by row" pins it.
- **(2) Not a (narrowing).** The rule that refuses a predicate write over 10,000 matched rows is the engine's existing `resolveBulkPerRowHookBudget` contract (spec `bulk-write-hook-conformance.ts`, D6). It already holds every object that carries a per-row after-hook, and this PR does not change it. Which objects carry such a hook is kernel composition, not a published accept-set. The audit plugin registers global `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` hooks (`audit-writers.ts:2885-2886`), so on a standard kernel every business object is already under the ceiling. A plugin adding a code hook, as audit, sharing and work-calendar do, has never been a narrowing. The new refusal is reachable only on a kernel with neither realtime nor audit, and the changeset and docs name it with its remedy. No dogfood is owed. The seat may overrule this if it reads composition otherwise.
- **(3) Restore.** That a restore is not re-indexed on such a kernel is stated in both the changeset and the docs. #38017 carries it, and that is right.

**Landing:** not governed, so the area lands it after ACCEPT.
